organizations.name: Dade Heritage Trust
organizations.overview: Founded in 1972, Dade Heritage Trust is Miami-Dade County's largest historic preservation organization, working to preserve the county's architectural, environmental, and cultural heritage through education and advocacy.

accomplishments.text: Was awarded a Florida Division of Historical Resources Small Matching Grant specifically to conduct a comprehensive survey of El Portal's historic resources.

organizations.name: Village of El Portal
organizations.overview: El Portal is a small village in Miami-Dade County, home to the El Portal Archaeological Zone — a Tequesta Native American mound and settlement site dating to roughly 200-600 AD, the first archaeological site publicly recognized and preserved in Miami-Dade County (designated 1983).

accomplishments.text: Officially designated the El Portal Seawall a historic site in 2008, recognizing it as a surviving example of early waterfront engineering tied to the village's development.

plannedActivities.text: As of a July 2024 Village Council meeting, the council was discussing how to restore and protect the eroding Sherwood Forest archaeological mound. No coverage found since then confirming whether this turned into an actual restoration effort or stalled — status as of today is unconfirmed, not verified-ongoing.
plannedActivities.linkLabel: LocalLens: El Portal mound preservation discussion (July 2024)

plannedActivities.text: The Sherwood Forest Archaeological Training Field School is running a 2026 season at this exact site, per the Archaeological Institute of America's fieldwork bulletin.

reviewNotes: Strongest hyperlocal hit rate of the four topics tested. The mound/seawall are literally in El Portal, a village of ~2,300 people — small-village-scale civic topics beat watershed-scale environmental ones on the 10-mile test, as predicted. Note: 'Village of El Portal' is a municipal government, not a 501(c)(3) — included on the same precedent as NYC Planning/NYC Buildings appearing in the original curated dataset as legitimate civic orgs. UPDATE from a recency check: the mound-preservation item downgraded from 'actively working to restore' to 'as of July 2024, was discussing' — no follow-up coverage confirms current status. The field school and seawall-designation items held up as genuinely dated and current/permanent respectively; the septic and Juneteenth items in the other two drafts also held up or improved. Net across all 'present' tense claims tested so far: 2 held up, 1 improved, 1 stale/unconfirmed (this one), 1 contradicted (food pantry hours), 1 was flat wrong (clean water draft, since corrected).
